cases.title: The Bus Stop Blast
cases.presentation: A small explosion at a bus stop. A police officer's radiation pager is alarming. 7 casualties: one with a partial leg amputation and arterial bleeding, others with fragment wounds.
cases.question: Best approach?
options: A: Standard PPE; tourniquet and triage now; remove patients' clothing; limit time near the seat of the blast; notify hospitals of contamination; decon as part of care.
B: Withdraw everyone until radiation is mapped.
D: Wait for Level A suits.
cases.explanation: RDDs injure mainly by blast. Radiation risk to patients and responders is usually low; treat life threats immediately, minimize time near the source, and decon by disrobing.
cases.clinicalPearl: Dirty bomb = bomb first, dirt second.

cases.title: Fever and Pustules
cases.presentation: A 30-year-old with 3 days of high fever and back pain now has firm pustules on the face, forearms, palms, and soles — all at the same stage.
cases.question: Your actions?
options: A: Transport by bus with others.
B: Ignore the rash — treat the fever.
D: Treat as possible smallpox: mask the patient, N95/PAPR + gown + gloves + eye protection, limit crew, notify medical control/public health, decon the vehicle.
cases.explanation: Synchronous centrifugal pustules including palms/soles = smallpox pattern. A single case is a public-health emergency.
cases.clinicalPearl: Same-stage pustules on palms and soles → think smallpox.

cases.title: Seven Burned Hands
cases.presentation: Over a week, a clinic sees seven scrap-metal workers with painful red skin lesions on their hands and nausea. No chemical history.
cases.question: Most likely explanation?
options: C: A lost radioactive source causing local radiation injury/ARS (exposure)
cases.explanation: Clusters of unexplained 'burns' + GI symptoms in people handling scrap suggest an orphan radioactive source (e.g., a medical teletherapy head). These patients are exposed, not necessarily contaminated.
cases.clinicalPearl: Unexplained burns in a cluster = think radiation.
